title: Cross-family harness integration (ref): the v0->v3 evolution + discoveries
desc: T3 reference tier. The night the gemini harness went from false-fail to precise hard-enforce: the version evolution, the discoveries, and the lessons. Parent: cross-family-harness-integration. Howto: cross-family-harness-integration-howto.
steps: EVOLUTION v0->v3 (2026-06-11, driven one user line at a time) -- v0 BROKEN: kih exit 2 -> gemini reads non-zero as 'Hook failed' -> scary warning + fallback permission prompt. v1 (Agent 4): $isGeminiFam && exit2 -> exit0 + append a WHOLE-TOOL one-shot deny to autonomy.toml (enforces but over-broad, so one-shot/cleanup-next-call). v2 (user 'add the harness PATTERN, deny precisely'): commandPrefix/commandRegex deny of the SPECIFIC command (ls still passes) -> precise -> can be PERSISTENT + deduped; symmetric APPROVE = find+delete the rule. v3 (user 'pre-guide so it does not retry'): on a block, emit ANTICIPATORY guidance to stderr -- the reason + the do-this-instead + an explicit 'do NOT retry, this is now policy-denied' -- so the AI redirects instead of burning cycles retrying a now-enforced block. v3 builds on the v2 relay (sequential, not parallel -- same file).

HARNESS-STRENGTHENING BACKLOG (2026-06-11 night findings -> fixes, the 'Hongik harness' gets stronger). (1) SANDBOX-SCOPE GAP: Test-WkIsCheapAgentSession + Test-WkHarnessSourceIsSandboxed (wkharness-common.ps1 ~L1168/1185) already sandbox cheap tiers from CANONICAL harness edits, but the WRAPPERS (Edit.ps1/Write.ps1/Agent.ps1/etc.) are NOT recognized as canonical (the protected list is only wkharness-guards/common/post/status), so a cheap session (Haiku) edited Edit.ps1 unblocked. FIX: extend the harness-source recognition to the wrapper names + the kih/tools/wrappers path. (2) STALE personal-docs REFS: the harness was migrated to the kih repo, but many refs (hook paths, symlink targets, dot-sources, skill SOURCE notes like codex-tool-wrappers) still point at D:/GitHub/personal-docs -- ALL stale-ref bugs. A Haiku full-audit is inventorying them; FIX = repoint to kih. (3) v2 AGY PRECISE-DENY BUG: the relay derives commandPrefix for gemini's run_shell_command but NOT agy's run_command (verified: agy git --no-verify block added a priority-900 deny with NO commandPrefix = whole-tool fallback). FIX: derive the command from the agy-adapted tool_input too. (4) PRIORITY RANGE: gemini autonomy.toml priority is 0-999; v1 used 2000 = a schema violation = likely INEFFECTIVE (v2 uses 900 -- so re-confirm the b47ybpqjd live block actually came from the rule and not yolo). (5) TIER-GATE CASCADE x3 this night: a fat T1 capture trips it AND a brief that READS a fat skill (codex-tool-wrappers score 0) blocks dispatch -- FIX: exempt already-tiered skills, judge the cluster, and 3-tier the fat ones (codex-tool-wrappers, claude-md-harness-rules T1). (6) GUARD FALSE-POSITIVE: a Remove-Item protection guard mis-parsed a regex fragment (\d+) in a PowerShell command as a path-to-remove -- the path extractor should not match inside quoted regex strings. META: every item here was found by VERIFYING (induce/parse) or by the user, never by trusting a green summary -- even Opus shipped 6+ of tonight's bugs, which is the whole point: the SYSTEM (audit/guard/verify/knowledge-tree), not any model's intelligence, is what catches them.

STALE-REF AUDIT RESULT + THE DIVERGENCE TRAP (2026-06-11, Haiku ab9237d found 30 refs / 13 critical). Critical repoints (personal-docs -> kih): (1) WKAppBot/bin 9 wrapper symlinks (Agent/Bash/Cmd/Edit/Glob/Grep/PowerShell/Read/Write .cmd) target personal-docs/tools; (2) D:/GitHub/wkharness-common.ps1 L9 dot-source; (3) ~/.claude/settings.json L31 audit-log.ps1 hook path; (4) kih/tools/wkharness-session-init.ps1 L424+L534 personalTools hardcoded var. Medium: kih/tools/gemini-pace.ps1 L132 log path. Low: SKILL.md docs (wkharness-guards 13 lines, harness-edit-write-skill-bypass 2, on-load-howto 1). THE TRAP that verify caught and the audit MISSED: kih AND personal-docs BOTH still hold the wrappers and they have DIVERGED -- Edit.ps1 is kih=78L vs personal-docs=87L (personal-docs carries Haiku's nudge edits + more), and wkharness-common.ps1 exists ONLY in kih (so the personal-docs dot-source target may be broken). A NAIVE repoint-to-kih would REGRESS (discard the newer personal-docs edits). REAL FIX SEQUENCE: (a) RECONCILE -- merge the newer personal-docs wrapper edits INTO kih so kih becomes the single canonical latest; (b) repoint the symlinks + dot-source + hook path to kih; (c) delete the personal-docs duplicates; verify a wrapper still runs after each step. Careful + verified, a fresh focused pass -- NOT a 7am buggy-Opus grind. META-LESSON: a cheap audit can be thorough at FINDING facts yet naive in its CONCLUSIONS -- Opus must verify the audit's recommendation, not just trust its inventory.

DOCTOR-AS-REPAIR-VEHICLE governance (user spec 2026-06-11). wkdoctor deploys BEFORE the harness (it is the SDK front-line tool that lands first), so ALL self-repair MAY run THROUGH the doctor -- it is the universal repair vehicle. MANDATORY GUARDS: (1) before operating, the doctor repair must CHECK the Hongik Harness (the canonical wkappbot-kih body) is INSTALLED -- never repoint or heal into a missing target. (2) PER-CLI healing fires ONLY when that CLI's own installation exists (do not heal an absent Claude / Codex / Gemini install). Applied to the wrapper-symlink repair (module 25-harness-symlink-canonical.ps1, detection LIVE, 8/8 symlinks confirmed stale): repoint WKAppBot/bin/<Name>.cmd from personal-docs to wkappbot-kih/tools ONLY IF kih/tools holds that wrapper, and sync the (live) personal-docs content into kih FIRST so the repoint does not regress the divergence (Edit.ps1 pd=87L newer than kih=78L incl tonight's nudge). REMAINING BUILD (verified-fresh): the guarded auto-repair + the session-init REINSTALL (re-point all wrapper symlinks to kih on every harness init). FORENSICS that justify the install-guard: a premature delete of personal-docs (eed7ef5) was REVERTED (98a9d38 'personal-docs was still LIVE') precisely because the symlinks were not repointed first -- the guard 'harness installed before repair' + 'repoint before delete' is what finally makes the personal-docs deletion safe. Also: session-init L424/534 still WRITES personal-docs hook paths each session = an active reinforce-loop to fix in the same pass.

DOCTOR GHA SELF-TEST mandate (user spec 2026-06-11): EVERY doctor operation -- every check AND every repair scenario -- must be TESTED on GitHub Actions across all processes + situations, and the workflow must be TRIGGERABLE on-demand (workflow_dispatch) on top of scheduled/push. Rationale = the night's thesis applied to the HEALER ITSELF: the doctor is the repair vehicle that touches the live system (symlinks, harness, per-CLI installs), so its destructive ops must be CI-verified in a sandbox BEFORE they ever run on a real machine. Build (verified-fresh): a windows-runner GHA workflow exercising the self-contained doctor self-test modules (21-sandbox-integrity, 22-guard-logic-selftests, 23-bintool-param-first, 25-harness-symlink-canonical) + synthetic repair scenarios; triggers = workflow_dispatch + push + schedule. wkdoctor-telemetry.yml already collects results; this is the TEST harness. THE COMPLETE DOCTOR-SYSTEM LOOP (this night's full blueprint): detect (modules) -> repair (guarded: harness-installed + per-CLI-install-exists, deployed-first as the universal vehicle) -> GHA-test (every op, every situation) -> on-demand trigger. Detection module 25 is LIVE; the guarded repair + session-init reinstall + GHA test-harness + the personal-docs->kih reconcile are the remaining verified-fresh build.

DIRECT-SPEC RESOLUTION and the forwarder SPOF (2026-06-11; extends step 4 doctor-as-repair-vehicle). INCIDENT: the D:\GitHub\wkharness*.ps1 hub forwarders (thin shim that redirects to kih) are a single point of failure -- a Gemini WILDCARD rm cleaning junk files deleted them AND the SDK repo .git top-level files; later a Haiku used dd to strip a BOM and DESTROYED wkharness-post.ps1. ROOT-CAUSE CLASS: any indirection file the wiring depends on is a deletion/corruption target. RESOLUTION (user: direct file spec, no symbolic reference): point ~/.claude/settings.json PreToolUse/PostToolUse DIRECTLY at D:\GitHub\wkappbot-kih\tools\wkharness.ps1 and wkharness-post.ps1 -- no forwarder, so for Claude nothing exists to delete/BOM/repair. install.ps1 preCmd/postCmd repointed to kih-direct (Write-Shim hub generation becomes dead weight for Claude). BOM ROOT CAUSE: install.ps1 AND install-gemini-policy.ps1 both wrote the hub with [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8 which EMITS a UTF-8 BOM, so every reinstall re-BOMd the forwarders and settings.json -- fixed to (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding(false)). TWO-WRITER CONFLICT: install.ps1 (dumb passthrough) and install-gemini-policy.ps1 (gemini adapter doing tool to tool_name) wrote the SAME D:\GitHub\wkharness.ps1 with different content, last writer winning -- that is why its content kept changing mid-session; gemini still needs its adapter so the hub file stays for gemini, but Claude must not depend on it. POWERSHELL.cmd SHADOW: where powershell resolved D:\GitHub\WKAppBot\bin\PowerShell.cmd (a Claude-named wrapper) BEFORE the real powershell.exe, so every wkXXX.cmd relay calling bare powershell hit the harness wrapper and died with No stdin JSON -- this broke wktasklist.cmd. FIX: remove the PowerShell.cmd/.ps1 wrappers and drop the PowerShell entry from wkharness-session-init.ps1 wrapper-reinstall array (the regen source). GIT WILDCARD-RM RECOVERY: when objects/refs/reflog survive but .git HEAD/config/index are deleted, recreate HEAD = ref refs/heads/main plus a minimal config (remote origin, branch tracking, lfs), then git reset --mixed rebuilds the index, then git ls-files -z --deleted piped to xargs -0 git checkout -- restores deleted tracked working-tree files (committed junk comes back too -- clean it deliberately, never by wildcard). DOCTOR EXPANSION (the remaining-build of step 4, in flight): modules 27 wiring-reinstall (settings drift triggers the call-operator on install.ps1), 28 forwarder-BOM, 29 powershell-shadow, 30 autonomy-toml-valid (the gemini TOML parse error -- a double-quoted commandPrefix holding a raw Windows backslash path is an invalid TOML escape; fix with single-quoted literal strings or strip the WK-PERSISTENT-DENY block), 31 git-integrity -- one wkdoctor run auto-detects and fixes every failure mode from this incident.

BACKLOG -- ANTICIPATORY PRE-FLIGHT ADVISORY (user 2026-06-11, next harness-strengthening idea). A BLOCKED tool call is the WORST token waste: the whole prompt plus the context cache must be re-sent to the server on retry. So do NOT only emit anticipatory guidance AT the block (v3) -- emit it BEFORE, in the PostToolUse hook of the PRECEDING tool, so the AI composes the next call correctly on the FIRST try. DESIGN: the post-hook inspects current state (pace tier, recent command hygiene, delegation intent) and, when the NEXT call is likely to hit a known gate, appends a short heads-up to the just-finished tool result. Examples: over-target -> next non-wk command will be wk-only-gated, use a wk tool or delegate; about-to-delegate -> the Agent brief needs Goal/Files/Approach/Constraints/Exit plus 3 skill reads (agent-on-load) plus run_in_background. This makes the post-hook a NEXT-MOVE COACH, converting cache-resend waste into one-shot success. Pairs with delegation-preflight-oneshot (the checklist) and gate-as-sign P5 (a block names its escape) -- this moves the sign UPSTREAM of the block.

ANTICIPATORY ADVISORY -- IDEAL FIRST TARGET = STALL (user 2026-06-11, refining the backlog above). The stall-guard is the BEST first implementation because, unlike predicting an arbitrary next block, its trip is a KNOWN COUNTDOWN: the harness already tracks the solo-run clock and the consecutive-non-wk call count. So the PostToolUse hook can emit a heads-up at a WARNING threshold (e.g. 80 percent of the window): stall in about N calls or M minutes, delegate or knowledge-ify NOW -- so the AI acts BEFORE the hard stall-block fires and never eats the cache-resend. Generalize: any gate whose state is a measurable countdown (the stall window, pace approaching 95 percent) is a clean anticipatory-advisory candidate; gates that depend on the unknown next-command CONTENT are harder and lower priority. Build order: wire the countdown gates (stall, pace-95) into the post-hook advisory first.
